sections.h2: What are the fastest ways to sell in Downers Grove, IL?
sections.html:
Speed points to a direct cash sale in Downers Grove, while a top price points to a broker listing and a house staged for showings. Handling the sale yourself falls in between.

  • A broker suits a house in good shape that can wait through showings and a buyer's loan.
  • Selling alone suits an owner who already knows the local price range.
  • Cash suits estates, houses that need a roof or new systems, occupied rentals and owners relocating on short notice.

At a middle home value of $449,800, each extra month of holding a house means more tax, insurance and utility cost, so the time a direct sale saves deserves a place in your comparison.

sections.h2: What is Downers Grove like for sellers?
sections.html:
Downers Grove is a DuPage County village roughly 20 miles from the Chicago Loop, between I-88 and I-55. Pierce Downer settled the area in 1832, and the name refers to the old bur oak grove around it. Burlington trains arrived in 1864, and the village incorporated in March 1873.

Metra's BNSF Line stops three times in the village, at Belmont Road, Main Street and Fairview Avenue, and the Grove Commuter Shuttle feeds two of those stations. I-355, I-88 and Ogden Avenue (U.S. 34) run through or beside the community. The village's 2023 financial report ranks Duly Health and Care, Hearthside Food Solutions, Advocate Good Samaritan Hospital and Midwestern University as the largest employers, and Dover and Univar Solutions are among the corporate headquarters.

Grade School District 58 runs most of the elementary and middle schools. Center Cass District 66 operates Prairieview, Elizabeth Ide and Lakeview Junior High, and Community High School District 99 covers Downers Grove North and South.

Mid-19th-century houses cluster near the center, and every later decade is represented around them. The village has had one of the Chicago area's highest teardown rates, with small older houses replaced by much larger ones. If your house is dated, tell buyers it may suit a rebuild as well as a move-in purchase.

sections.h2: What local history and green space shape Downers Grove?
sections.html:
The Lyman Home, built in 1839 by the Rev. Orange Lyman and his wife, is believed to be the first house in the village and served as a stop on the Underground Railroad. In April 1947 a Burlington Twin Cities Zephyr struck a tractor that had fallen from a freight train and crashed into the Main Street Station, killing three people. The village has been named a Tree City USA 28 times by the National Arbor Day Foundation, and two forest preserves, Lyman Woods and Maple Grove, lie inside its borders.

The village covers about 14.5 square miles, a larger footprint than most DuPage towns except Bartlett, Aurora, Naperville and Bolingbrook. Its population rose from 47,833 in 2010 to 50,247 in 2020. The village's climate record shows a high of 105 degrees in July 2005 and a low of minus 26 in January 1985, and about 38 inches of precipitation in a typical year, with August the wettest month.

Education runs deep here: Midwestern University trains osteopathic physicians, pharmacists and dentists, and the private Avery Coonley School, founded in 1906, has been at its present site since 1929. The village's wastewater is treated by the Downers Grove Sanitary District.

sections.h2: Why do teardowns and stormwater come up in Downers Grove?
sections.html:
Teardowns have been contentious because larger new houses cover more of each lot and push rainwater into neighboring yards and streets, and critics also say they thin out affordable housing. The village's permit page lists summaries of its stormwater and tree protection ordinance changes plus site-management forms such as a construction checklist and a notice to adjacent property owners.

Three practical effects follow for a seller:

  • A buyer planning to rebuild must follow the village's demolition, stormwater and tree rules, so ask Community Development which apply to your lot.
  • Drainage history on your lot matters, so disclose known water problems.
  • Open permits or unfinished work should be closed out before listing.

The permit page also carries residential re-roofing requirements, a contractor list, an encroachment license, a pool information sheet and a form for homeowners acting as their own plumbing contractor, so a buyer planning a new roof, a pool or DIY plumbing has a place to start. Sellers who made such changes should have their permit paperwork on hand.

The village runs a permit portal through its Customer Self Service system, and its Stormwater Utility and Utility Bill services are separate accounts to settle at sale.

sections.h2: How does DuPage County property tax work for a Downers Grove seller?
sections.html:
DuPage County collects in arrears, so the 2025 tax year was billed and paid in 2026. The Treasurer mailed 321,773 bills on April 29, each with two coupons, and the due dates were June 1 and September 1, 2026.

In the Treasurer's letter, the general homestead and senior exemptions are each listed at $8,000, and owners are urged to confirm that every exemption they qualify for appears on the bill. A yellow box means a mortgage company is paying, so a second check would be a duplicate. The Treasurer does not set values; the assessor named on your bill answers those questions. Call 630-407-5900 for payment issues.

At closing, your title company can explain how the year's tax is divided. The state's rate under 35 ILCS 200/31-10 is 50 cents per $500 of value or fraction, and the same company can say whether a county or local stamp also applies. For current recording fees, ask the DuPage County Clerk's recording division.

sections.h2: What should a Downers Grove owner prepare before an offer arrives?
sections.html:
Preparation prevents surprises at the table.

  1. Find the deed and confirm every name on it will sign.
  2. Print the newest tax bill and see which exemptions it shows.
  3. Ask the village about open permits and finish any unfinished work.
  4. Settle the village utility account before the house changes hands.
  5. Obtain a written payoff from each lender or lienholder.

If you inherited the house, gather the paperwork that shows who may sign early, since a title company will ask for it. List or sell directly, but judge each offer by the net after payoffs, taxes and closing costs, and get terms in writing.

faqs.q: Which county is Downers Grove in?
faqs.a: DuPage County. Property tax bills come from the DuPage County Treasurer and deeds are recorded with the county.

faqs.q: When do DuPage property taxes fall due?
faqs.a: They are billed a year behind. For tax year 2025 the installments fell on June 1 and September 1, 2026, on one bill with two coupons.

faqs.q: Can I sell a Downers Grove house to a builder who will tear it down?
faqs.a: Yes. Teardown buyers are common in the village. Share what you know about drainage or trees on the lot, and point them to the village's stormwater, tree protection and demolition requirements.

faqs.q: Which school districts serve Downers Grove?
faqs.a: Most of the village is in Grade School District 58, some areas are in Center Cass District 66, and the two high schools are in Community High School District 99. Check your tax bill to see which districts your parcel pays.

faqs.q: How can I avoid paying my tax bill twice?
faqs.a: Check for the yellow box on your bill. It says when a mortgage company is paying, and in that case you should not send another payment.
